chat.title: Chat
chat.intro: Ask an agent a question and get an answer with its sources attached.
chat.howToLabel: How do I use this screen?
howTo: Pick an agent at the top — each one has its own knowledge base and its own tools.
Type your question; the answer streams in and lists the sources it used underneath.
Use the thumbs buttons under an answer to leave feedback — it is recorded in Langfuse.
chat.emptyDesc: Starting a chat needs at least one active agent. Enable one under Admin > Agents.
chat.startersHeading: What can you ask this agent?

support_copilot.q1: How do I cancel my order?
support_copilot.q2: How many days does a refund take?
support_copilot.q3: Where do I find my tracking number?

analytics.q1: Which region sold the most in the last 30 days?
analytics.q2: How is total revenue split across regions?

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.uploadPrompt: Choose a file to upload into this collection.
knowledge.intro: The documents agents ground their answers in live here.
knowledge.howToLabel: How do I use this screen?
howTo: Pick a collection on the left; each has its own sensitivity level and retention rule.
Upload a document — the system extracts the text, flags personal data, chunks it and makes it searchable.
Once the status reads 'Ready' the document can be cited in Chat.
knowledge.emptyCollectionsDesc: A collection is the box that groups documents by sensitivity and retention rule. The first ones come from `make seed`, or an admin creates them.
knowledge.emptyDocumentsDesc: Add the first one with 'Upload document' above; processing starts in the background as soon as the upload finishes.

approvals.title: My Approvals
approvals.intro: Anything an agent wants to send outside the company waits here until you decide.
approvals.howToLabel: How do I use this screen?
howTo: Each row is an agent's paused step — the action has not happened yet.
Review the payload; use 'Edit payload' to change it before it goes out.
Approving resumes the run and the action really happens; rejecting cancels it.
approvals.emptyDesc: When an agent attempts an action that leaves the company (sending an email, for instance) a row appears here and waits for your decision.
approvals.whyWaiting: This step is an action that leaves the company; Fleet never runs one on its own — it asks a person first.

home.intro: Fleet as it stands today: what is waiting for approval, what automations ran, and which agents you can talk to.
home.howToLabel: How do I use this screen?
howTo: The tiles above show only the numbers your role can see; each one links to the screen that acts on it.
Go to Chat to ask a question, or to Examples to try a ready-made task.
Go to Automations to run one by hand or to define a new one.
home.tileSpendHint: Model cost over the last 24 hours
home.noRunsDesc: Run an automation by hand from the Automations screen and its result shows up here.
home.noAgentsDesc: A chat cannot start until an agent is active. Enable one under Admin > Agents.

scenarios.intro: The agent scenarios each department has today, and the ones still on the way.
scenarios.howToLabel: How do I use this screen?
howTo: Cards tagged 'Live' can be tried today; the link on the card takes you straight to that agent.
'Coming soon' cards name the sprint they land in.
To see what a scenario actually does, use the ready-made inputs on the Examples screen.

automations.title: Automations
automations.n8nDown: The automation system (n8n) is currently unreachable. Please notify your admin or try again later.
automations.n8nAuthError: Could not connect to the automation system — the API key is missing or invalid. Contact your admin.
automations.invoiceIntakeDesc: Upload an invoice image; the system extracts the fields and sends them for your approval.
automations.invoiceUploadHint: Choose a PNG, JPEG, or WEBP image (max 10MB).
automations.weeklySummaryDesc: Posts the last 7 days' sales summary to Slack.
automations.runQueuedForApproval: Invoice queued — check the Approvals page.
automations.runInactive: This automation is currently inactive — activate it first.
automations.runUnreachable: Could not reach the automation system.
automations.intro: Scheduled and manually triggered automations; all of them execute on n8n.
automations.howToLabel: How do I use this screen?
howTo: If a card reads 'Active' the automation runs on its own when its trigger fires.
'Run now' triggers it without waiting; the outcome appears on the 'Last run' line.
Use 'New automation' to define your own — steps that leave the company still go through approval.
automations.emptyDesc: An automation is a trigger (a schedule or a manual run) plus a list of steps. Define your first one with 'New automation'.
automations.deleteConfirm: Delete this automation? Its n8n counterpart is removed too.
automations.deployFailed: The automation was saved but could not be deployed to n8n. Check that n8n is running and save it again.

examples.title: Examples
examples.subtitle: Try sample tasks for each agent, or add your own example.
examples.question: Question
examples.pendingApproval: Pending approval — go to the Approvals page.
examples.intro: Ready-made sample tasks for each agent — the fastest way to try the platform.
examples.howToLabel: How do I use this screen?
howTo: Pick an agent at the top and press 'Try it' on an example.
Examples are real runs: steps that leave the company still land in the approval queue.
An example you add yourself shows up in the same list for everyone.
examples.emptyDesc: Write the first one with 'Add example' — what you add is visible to everyone else too.

admin.title: Admin
admin.noAccess: You do not have access to this page.
admin.globalReadOnlyDesc: When enabled, blocks every agent's external write actions.
admin.clearanceLegend: public < internal < confidential < pii — a model may only serve requests at or below its clearance; no cloud model is ever cleared for pii (TRD §8).
admin.keyShownOnce: This key is shown only once — save it somewhere safe.
admin.name: Name
admin.budgetCreateError: Could not create budget — one may already exist for this scope and period.
admin.budgetWarningBanner: Budgets over their soft or hard limit:
admin.intro: Platform settings: agents, models, users, budgets and services.
admin.howToLabel: How do I use this screen?
howTo: Tabs appear according to your role — Agents is open to builders, the rest to platform admins.
A model's sensitivity clearance decides which data that model is allowed to see.
The Services tab shows the live health and local addresses of the whole stack.
admin.emptyAgentsDesc: An agent is a prompt, a model and a tool list. Add one with 'New agent', or load the demo agents with `make seed`.
admin.emptyModelsDesc: A model entry names a model on the LiteLLM gateway and its sensitivity clearance. Start with 'Add model'.
admin.emptyUsersDesc: Users are created in Keycloak and appear here on first sign-in. `make seed` loads the demo users.
admin.emptyKeysDesc: An API key is how a service such as n8n identifies itself to Fleet. Create one with 'Issue key' — the value is shown only once.
admin.emptyBudgetsDesc: A budget caps monthly or daily spend for a department, agent or user. Add one with 'Create budget'.
admin.emptyAuditDesc: An audit entry is written on every API request. Loosen the filters, or do a few things in the app and look again.
admin.servicesFooter: These credentials are for the local development stack only; they are read from the environment and never committed.

writeExternal.definition: A write that leaves the company (sending an email, opening a PR). Fleet never runs one on its own — it goes to the approval queue first.

sensitivityPii.definition: The content contains personal data. These requests are routed to local models only and never reach a cloud model (KVKK).

riskClass.definition: The risk label every tool carries: read, write:internal, or write:external. It is what decides whether an approval is required.

hitl.definition: Human-in-the-loop: at a risky step the run pauses, a person reviews it and approves or rejects. The rows on the Approvals screen are those pauses.

services.revealRestricted: Plaintext credentials are shown to platform admins only; here they stay masked.
services.emptyDesc: The Fleet API could not be reached. Check that it is running (`make api`) and try again.
services.purposeUnknown: No description written for this service yet.
services.optionalHintGeneric: This service is not part of the default stack; being down is normal.

optionalHint.ollama: Needed for the local model lane (KVKK). Start it with `make dev PROFILE=ollama` or the Ollama app itself.
optionalHint.arq: The worker that drains the document-processing queue. Start it with `uv run arq fleet_rag.ingest.worker.WorkerSettings`.

purpose.postgres: The platform's main database: users, agents, collections, approvals, the spend ledger and the audit log.
purpose.redis: Rate limiting, the semantic cache, and the job queues (RAG ingest, n8n queue mode) all live here.
purpose.qdrant: Vectors for document chunks — what RAG search actually reads.
purpose.minio: Object store holding the raw uploaded files (S3-compatible).
purpose.keycloak: Authentication and role management; the web app and the API trust the tokens it issues.
purpose.litellm: The gateway every LLM call goes through — model routing, budgets and cost accounting happen here.
purpose.ollama: The local model lane: requests carrying personal data only ever reach models on this machine.
purpose.langfuse: LLM traces: prompt, response, cost and latency for every call.
purpose.alertmanager: Routes Prometheus alerts to channels such as Slack.
purpose.mailpit: Development SMTP box: email an agent sends never leaves the machine, it lands here.
purpose.n8n-main: The automation editor and its REST API; stores workflows and enqueues executions.
purpose.n8n-worker: The worker process that actually runs the queued automation executions.
purpose.arq: The worker that runs after a document upload: text extraction, OCR, PII scan, chunking and embedding.
purpose.promtail: The agent that collects container logs and pushes them to Loki — Loki's only source of data.

builder.title: New automation
builder.intro: Pick a trigger and a few steps; Fleet turns it into a workflow that runs on n8n.
builder.howToLabel: How do I use this screen?
howTo: Give the automation a name first — it becomes the identity of the workflow in n8n and cannot be changed later.
Choose the trigger: scheduled (runs by itself at set times) or manual (only when you run it).
Add steps in order. Use {{steps.step_id.field}} in a later step to reuse an earlier step's output.
Optionally add a condition: one set of steps runs when it holds, another when it does not.
Read what it will do in plain language with 'Preview', then save. Saving deploys it to n8n; you still have to activate it before it runs.
builder.name: Name
builder.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. It becomes the workflow's identity in n8n.
builder.nameLocked: The name is the workflow's identity in n8n and cannot be changed.
builder.triggerManualHint: Runs only when you press 'Run now' on the Automations screen.
builder.triggerScheduleHint: Runs by itself at the times you choose; you can still trigger it by hand.
builder.referenceHint: Reuse an earlier step's output in a later one with {{steps.step_id.field}}. No other kind of expression is accepted.
builder.previewHint: Read what the automation will do with 'Preview' before saving it.
builder.previewError: The automation is not valid. Check the fields.
builder.saved: Automation saved and deployed to n8n.
builder.savedButNotDeployed: Automation saved but could not be deployed to n8n.
builder.writeExternalWarning: This automation has a step that leaves the company; when it runs it will not send directly, it lands in the approval queue.

query.label: Database query
query.help: Runs a read-only SQL query. The table allowlist, row limit and timeout are the same ones the Analytics agent gets.

run.label: Ask an agent
run.help: Asks an agent a question and makes its answer available to later steps.

post.label: Post to Slack
post.help: Posts a message to an allowlisted Slack channel.

send.label: Send an email
send.help: Does not send directly: it lands in the approval queue and goes out once a person approves it.

notify.label: Record a note
notify.help: Sends nothing outside the company; leaves a note in the audit log.

templates.heading: Ready-made automations
templates.intro: Start from a working example instead of a blank form. Picking a template fills the form in; rename it and edit the fields before saving.

weeklySalesDigest.title: Weekly sales digest
weeklySalesDigest.description: Every Monday morning, totals the last 7 days of sales by region and posts a summary to the #weekly-summary Slack channel.

refundWatch.title: Refund watch
refundWatch.description: Counts refunded orders each morning. It messages #dev-agent only when there are any — a quiet day sends nothing.

agentBriefing.title: Daily analytics briefing
agentBriefing.description: Puts the same question to the Analytics agent each morning and records the answer in the audit log. Nothing leaves the platform.

monthlyReport.title: Monthly report email
monthlyReport.description: Emails a sales summary on the first of the month. The email is not sent straight away: it queues in Approvals and goes out once you approve it.

guide.title: Guide
guide.intro: Short paths showing how Fleet's screens connect: ask a question, add knowledge, build an automation, and watch the approval gate work.
howTo: Pick one of the paths below — each says how long it takes.
Read the steps, then use the button to go straight to that screen.
If a term is unfamiliar, check the glossary at the bottom of the page.
guide.glossaryIntro: The four terms in Fleet's screens that are platform vocabulary rather than plain English.

askAgent.title: Ask an agent a question
askAgent.intro: The shortest path: ask an agent something and see which document the answer came from.
askAgent.s1: Open Chat and pick support_copilot from the list at the top.
askAgent.s2: Click one of the suggested questions — it drops into the composer.
askAgent.s3: Send it and watch the answer stream in.
askAgent.s4: Check the source count under the answer — the agent did not invent this, it read it from the knowledge base.

addKnowledge.title: Add a document to the knowledge base
addKnowledge.intro: You decide what the agents answer from. Once your document is processed it shows up as a source in answers.
addKnowledge.s2: Pick a collection and upload a PDF or text file.
addKnowledge.s3: Wait for the status to move from processing to ready — the document is chunked, scanned for personal data and indexed.
addKnowledge.s4: Go back to Chat and ask about something in it; the new document should appear among the answer's sources.

buildAutomation.title: Build an automation
buildAutomation.intro: Set up a scheduled job that reads data, summarises it and posts to Slack. No code — a form.
buildAutomation.s1: Start from the Weekly sales digest template — the form arrives filled in.
buildAutomation.s2: Read the steps: one query, one Slack message. Edit the text if you like.
buildAutomation.s3: Use Preview to read what it will do in plain language.
buildAutomation.s4: Save it — the automation is deployed to n8n.
buildAutomation.s5: Hit Run now and see the result on the card; you don't have to wait for the cron.

approvalFlow.title: See the approval gate
approvalFlow.intro: Anything that reaches outside the platform — an email, a write to another system — is never done directly. This path shows that wall working.
approvalFlow.s1: Open the Monthly report email template — it contains an email step.
approvalFlow.s2: Notice the needs approval warning beside that step in the form.
approvalFlow.s3: Save it and hit Run now.
approvalFlow.s4: Go to Approvals: no email was sent, it queued, and the row says why it is waiting.
approvalFlow.s5: Approve it; only then does the action complete.
